title: Steady work in Minneapolis: South Side Ballroom and hotels
summary: The Young band plays weekends at the South Side Ballroom and at the Radisson and St. Paul hotels, singing Ain't She Sweet, and gets most of the good work.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Then he started booking things, then we started working in Minneapolis, man. We got work. We played all the time. Every weekend we was playing at a place called the South Side Ballroom. I think I mentioned something about that before,
about he was playing there -- when you was talking about Hines, and he was playing with somebody...

Rook Ganz. One of them. Well, we used to play there all the time. And the Radisson Hotel, and the St. Paul Hotel -- we played all of them. Because we had a good band -- I mean, a good entertaining band. And we used to sing together. Oh yeah, I forgot another tune we used to play -- "Ain't She Sweet." We used to sing that together.
That was with the family group.

No. This was with the dance band. "Ain't She Sweet." We used to sing that together, you know what I mean. We had a little novelty we used to put on it, and do a little selling(?). We were a pretty big name in Minneapolis, you know, because we got most of the good work... See, at that time in Minneapolis, there wasn't no big bands there -- not no big white bands. The only thing they had was five pieces playing a club...
